Everything good was once imagined and many other quotes were along those similar lines. And then rather than just being fearful of the things that I'm worried about for society and for humanity, I started to think what would the alternative be? What is that vision that I would love to see us have basic human needs for all global education being a basic human right that everyone experiences all the really important things that we want as humanity. And again, using vision and using imagination and just dreaming about the future. And I find it really fascinating in my day-to-day by literally having it beside me as I work every day, the little tiny decisions that can kind of help to angle towards that future that we want and can I help will any of that into existence? I honestly don't know. (00:57:24): But I feel like just by starting to write it down some little brainstorm exercise with a number of other people and starting to just etch out, how do we get closer and closer to that. On my vision of the future, it's community. It's the whole of humanity trying to dream bigger and to dream bigger goals. And then us actually rising to that occasion in the world. We don't want, I think loneliness is rife, purpose is gone. What we teach people in schools is pointless. And in my vision for 2050, it's none of those things. Communities are bound to fall. We all have deep purpose. And that deep purpose springs from having bigger dreams that we collectively go out and achieve. Something that we're doing at our Canva world to a keynote in two weeks time, which I think is going to be after this is released, we've been asking people what is one goal you'd like to see the world achieved in our lifetime? (00:58:25): And then people literally writing it down I think is pretty powerful. And then people sharing that with other people I think is pretty powerful. And then us actually figuring out how the hell do we turn? That reality that we all deeply desperately want into existence, I think is genuinely one of the biggest questions of our time. But then again, rather than trying to tackle that entire thing by yourself, how do you take that first tiny step that starts to see that in your own life, in your own family, in your own community? And I think that's where we'll get purpose from and I think that is one of the key answers to loneliness is actually working towards something bigger than yourself.
turns.zh:
我来解释一下为什么我会创作愿景板，因为这件事最近才发生。我确实觉得人类正处在一列失控的列车上。这列火车如果把许多不同公司的愿景、正在发生的各种事物快进50年，或者展望2050年时问自己："我们的世界是否更安全了？这个世界是否是我们希望孩子成长的乐土？这是否是我们理想的人类社会？"我不觉得我们正行驶在一条美好的轨道上。事实上，出于种种原因，这让我感到非常恐惧。因此，我静坐思考这种情绪片刻后，便开始着手创作我的2050愿景墙，从混乱走向清晰。  
（00:56:22）首先，我专注于我的2050愿景墙。我真的很喜欢这面墙，整面墙都贴满了引语。每一句美好的话语都曾是想象的产物，还有许多类似的引语。与其仅仅对社会和人类现状感到担忧，我开始思考：替代方案会是什么？我理想中的愿景是人人享有基本人类需求，全球教育成为人人都能体验的基本权利，实现我们作为人类共同渴望的重要目标。再次通过运用想象力和梦想未来，每天工作时将它置于身旁，我发现日常中的微小决策都能助力我们朝着理想的未来前行。我能否将其中一些变为现实？说实话，我不确定。  
（00:57:24）但我觉得只要开始与他人一起写下这些想法，进行头脑风暴，逐步规划如何一步步接近目标就足够了。在我的未来愿景中，关键是社区。是全人类共同努力放大梦想、追逐更远大目标。然后我们在全球范围内共同实现这些目标。我认为当前的孤独感普遍存在，人们失去了人生方向感。我们在学校教给人们的东西毫无意义。在我对2050年的愿景中，这些问题都不会存在。社区必将崛起，人们将拥有深刻的使命感，而这种使命感源于共同追逐更远大梦想并将其变为现实。  
（00:58:25）两周后在Canva全球大会上（可能在本文发布后），人们被问到："你希望在有生之年看到世界实现哪一个目标？"然后人们把答案写下来，这真的很震撼。再让人们与他人分享这些目标，意义非凡。如何将我们深切渴望的现实变为现实，确实是我们这个时代最重大的问题之一。但与其独自面对整个挑战，不如从微小的一步开始，在自己的生活、家庭和社区中践行这些目标。我认为这正是我们能找到人生意义的关键所在，也是对抗孤独感的关键答案。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. I really appreciate you sharing all that. I was thinking as you're talking, just considering how wildly successful Canva has been and just how ambitious that was when you started. I would not be at all surprised that this actually happens and that you achieve this very difficult vision.
turns.zh: 哇。真的很感谢你分享这么多内容。你在讲话时，我一直在思考Canva取得的巨大成功，以及你创业之初的雄心壮志。如果这真的能实现，如果你能实现这个极具挑战性的愿景，我一点也不感到惊讶。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: It's not something that I alone can achieve. I think it has to be obviously a global collective effort because there's zero chance I can go and achieve basic human needs for all. But I think that I'd like to change that. I'd like to help change the mood. I'd like to help change the way we're thinking about things. I genuinely think we need to move course a little and decide not what are all the things that we... what's the freight train we're currently on, but what is it that we actually want? What do we want our societies to look like? What do we want the world to look like? Is it good enough that there's people, hundreds of millions of people that can't eat? What the hell? It just literally makes no sense.
turns.zh: 这不是我一个人能做到的。我认为这显然需要全球性的共同努力，因为我绝不可能去满足全人类的基本需求。但我想改变这一现状。我想改变人们的思维方式。我真心认为我们需要稍微调整方向，别再纠结于我们当前所处的「货运列车」，而是去思考我们真正想要什么？我们希望我们的社会是什么样子？我们希望世界变成什么样子？当数亿人还吃不饱饭时，这怎么能说得通？简直太离谱了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A column B world, you might say.
turns.zh: 你可以说，这是一个"B世界"。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Melanie, this was incredible. Before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that you wanted to share? Anything else you want to leave listeners with?
turns.zh: 梅兰妮，你今天的分享太精彩了。在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前，你还有什么想和听众分享的吗？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: You have been extremely extensive. I don't think I've got anything else to add, frankly.
turns.zh: 你已经分享得非常全面了。说实话，我没什么要补充的了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's the goal. That's the goal. With that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. Melanie, are you ready?
turns.zh: 这才是目标。这才是目标。接下来，让我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节。梅兰妮，你准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: Let's go.
turns.zh: 开始吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: First question, what are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
turns.zh: 第一个问题，请推荐两到三本你最常向别人推荐的书？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: One of the books I love is The Power of Moments, and it talks, am I supposed to be really fast and not tell you about it?
turns.zh: 我喜欢的书之一是《关键时刻的力量》，不过我得快点说，不然就没时间了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's all good.
turns.zh: 没关系。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: Okay. Two books, the Power of Moments, and one of the books early on I read was Designing the Obvious, which I found very insightful.
turns.zh: 好的。两本书，《关键时刻的力量》，还有我早期读过的一本《设计显而易见》，我觉得非常有启发。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I like they shifted to fast mode. You don't have to go superfast. All good. What is a favorite product you've recently discovered that you really love? Not Canva.
turns.zh: 我喜欢他们切换到快速模式。你不必太快。没关系。接下来，你最近发现并特别喜欢的产品是什么？不是Canva。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: I love the Calm app. It is my daily companion. I use it to meditate. I use it to listen to music. I just find it very calming.
turns.zh: 我喜欢Calm应用程序。它是我的日常伴侣。我用它来冥想，用它来听音乐。我觉得它非常让人放松。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. First question. I usually ask about movies and TV shows. I hear you don't watch a lot because you're so busy and have so much going on. So I'm going to try it, new question I haven't asked before. I'm curious where this goes. So excluding Canva, what's a product you'd love to work on someday, whether it's like an existing other company like, "Oh, I wish I could work on that thing," or just a new product you'd love to build maybe after the Canva chapter.
turns.zh: 好的。第一个问题。我通常会问电影和电视节目的问题，但听说你因为太忙没时间看。所以我试试新问题，我之前没问过的。我很好奇结果如何。除了Canva，未来你最想参与开发的产品是什么？无论是现有公司的产品，比如“真希望能参与那个项目”，还是未来可能创建的新产品。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: I feel like my Canva chapter's going to go on for a long time, so I don't know, because we've got-
turns.zh: 我觉得我的Canva篇章还会持续很久，所以我也不确定，因为我们已经有——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: On the side, on the side.
turns.zh: 额外的，额外的计划，而且我们的计划已经很全面了。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: ... decent plans side and we're pretty extensive.
turns.zh: ...不错的额外计划，我们已经做得非常全面了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, maybe a company you'd love to fund. There we go.
turns.zh: 好的，或许有一家你乐意投资的公司。就这样吧。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: I feel like there's a lot of opportunity to create global infrastructure that is truly empowering. And so as I look at my 2050 wall, I think there's a lot of things that are currently only exclusively available to a small number of people that should be available to everyone. And so the more that we can do to uplift the rising tide lifts all boats I think is a thing that's just so of such critical importance. And I think there is this weird belief that you can be fine and everyone else can be not fine and that's all cool. I don't think that's cool. I think everyone suffers in such a case. So I think more things that help everyone to rise.
turns.zh: 我觉得有很多机会去创建真正能赋能全球的基础设施。当我审视我的2050年愿景时，我认为当前只有少数人能享有的服务，应该让所有人都能使用。因此，我们越能提升整体水平，就越能实现“水涨船高”的局面。我认为有一种奇怪的观念，认为自己过得好，而其他人过得不好，然后觉得这没什么大不了的。我不认同这种观点。我认为在这种情况下，每个人都会受损。所以我希望能有更多助力所有人崛起的事物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Maybe along those lines, but maybe not, is there a life motto that you find yourself coming back to and work your own life?
turns.zh: 或许是这个方向，或许不是，但你有没有一条人生格言，时常回想并指导自己生活？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: There's a few. I love the quote, happiness is when what you think, what you say and what you do are in harmony. I feel like that's a constant aspiration. And then I've just been so obsessed lately with the idea that everything is led by imagination. That imagination is the very first step of that creative process. So everything is good because once imagined is a quote you're going to be seeing from Canva all the time now because it is true that if you don't imagine it, you can't will it into existence. And in fact, everything great that we experience in life was first imagined.
turns.zh: 有几条。我很喜欢这句话：幸福就是你的所思、所言、所行三者和谐统一。我觉得这是一种持续的追求。最近我一直痴迷于一个观点：一切都由想象力引领。想象力是创意过程的第一步。所以一切皆有可能，因为一旦有了想象，你就能将它变为现实。事实上，我们生活中所经历的一切美好事物，最初都是想象出来的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. There's so much power to that one thought nugget there is just, there's all these tools now that can make building so much easier. You can just build anything you want, just describe it. But so many people are just like, I'm in the same boat. I'm just stuck. "What do I want?" I don't even don't know what I need. What should I build? And that's exactly what you're talking about there. Okay. Last question. So I saw it somewhere that you were an aspiring figure skater in your early years in high school, you had to wake up at 4:30 A.M. to practice. Is there something you learned from that period of your life that was helpful in building Canva?
turns.zh: 哇。这一个核心思想蕴含着巨大的力量。现在有许多工具能让构建变得容易得多。你只需描述，就能建造出任何你想要的东西。但很多人却深有共鸣，觉得自己也处境相似，停滞不前。“我想要什么？” 甚至不知道自己需要什么。应该建造什么？这正是你所谈到的。好的，最后一个问题。听说你高中早期曾是位有抱负的花样滑冰选手，每天早上4:30就得起床练习。这些经历对你创立Canva有什么帮助吗？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: So many things are quite directly applicable, falling down over and over again and getting up and trying again, the importance of hard work and determination. I think the falling down, it was quite literal in my figure skating in days, and maybe it was a little more metaphorical in today, but it is constant.
turns.zh: 有很多直接适用的经验，比如一次又一次地跌倒，然后爬起来再试一次，努力和决心的重要性。我觉得跌倒的经历，在我花样滑冰的日子里是字面意义上的跌倒，而如今可能更具隐喻意义，但这种精神始终如一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You're right. I wonder what that metaphor is for figure skating. I don't know. Anyway, Melanie, this was incredible. I am so thankful that you agreed to do this. Two final questions: where can folks find you if they want to maybe reach out, send you feedback on Canvas or join Canva, and how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 没错。我好奇花样滑冰的这个隐喻是什么。我不知道。不管怎样，梅兰妮，这次交流太棒了。非常感谢你愿意参与。最后两个问题：如果听众想联系你、给Canva反馈或加入Canva，可以在哪里找到你？他们如何能为你提供帮助？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: Really great questions. So you can find me on LinkedIn. That's where I post the most. And you can go to and I can get the URL to give us your wishes and we want to hear them and we literally listen to them. It doesn't just go into a suggestion box. And then how can they be helpful? Use Canva, spread Canva, teach Canva. We're doing a Canva World Tour through October, which is probably going to be updated when this is posted. (01:04:43): Come to our events. We do events all around the world and we'd love to see you and to hear from you. And if you are in a company, starting a company, try and do the 1% pledge. Try and figure out your own version of the two-step plan and try and build products and in every decision that you make that actually makes the world that you want to live in. I think there's this kind of belief sometimes that the world is created by other people, but we all have a very active hand in creating the world that we live in. And every decision that you make for investors, every company that you fund, is that contributing the world to the world that you want to live in? Or is it creating the freight train that none of us want to be on?
turns.zh: 这些问题真是太棒了。大家可以在领英上找到我，那是我最常发布内容的地方。你们可以访问我的领英主页，我会把链接发给你们，让你们畅所欲言。我们真的会认真倾听这些建议，而不是把它们塞进建议箱。那么，这些建议如何能真正带来帮助呢？首先，使用Canva、推广Canva、教授Canva。我们从现在到10月份会开展Canva全球巡回活动，后续会更新相关信息。（01:04:43）：欢迎来参加我们的活动。我们在全球各地举办活动，很期待与大家见面交流。如果你身处一家公司，或者正在创业，不妨尝试“1%承诺”计划。想办法制定自己的两步计划，打造产品。无论你做何种决策，都要致力于构建一个你理想中的世界。有时人们认为世界是由他人创造的，但我们每个人都对创造自己所生活的世界负有积极责任。你为投资者做出的每个决策、资助的每个公司项目，是否在为你理想中的世界添砖加瓦？还是在助长我们都不愿身处的混乱局面？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I have to ask before I let you go. Are you going to have the rap dancers at the next Canva event?
turns.zh: 在结束之前我得问问，下次Canva活动还会请说唱舞者吗？

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: You'll have to wait and see.
turns.zh: 你们就等着瞧吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay. Melanie, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 好的。梅兰妮，非常感谢你今天的到来。

turns.speaker: Melanie Perkins
turns.en: Thank you so much, Lenny, for having me and your great well-researched questions.
turns.zh: 莱尼，非常感谢你邀请我，也感谢你精心准备的问题。
